subject: Re: Contract ask — termination rights & beyond-credits remedies
messages:
From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@optihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: OptiHealth Procurement <procurement@optihealth.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: termination rights + remedies beyond credits (SLA)

Hi Marissa / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we work internal approvals for the Redwood pilot, procurement has pushed back on the SLA clause. Their ask is that, in addition to service credits, OptiHealth have: (1) a termination right for repeated P99 latency misses, and (2) a liquidated damages / fee-at-risk structure (we proposed up to 2x monthly committed fees for a material breach) rather than credits alone.

High level context: we are integrating Redwood into customer-facing clinical workflows — uptime and tail latency directly affect patient experience. Our legal and compliance teams are not comfortable with credits as the sole remedy for sustained SLO breaches.

I've attached a short spreadsheet (OptiHealth_SLA_ask.xlsx) that maps triggers to remedies. We know this is beyond your standard offering, but wanted to surface it early to see options.

Questions for Redwood:
- Would Redwood consider a staged remedy (credits -> fee at risk -> termination) with cure periods?
- If termination is required, can you entertain a cap on aggregated liability and a clear cure window to avoid spurious terminations?
- Any precedent you can share for enterprise customers?

We'd like to finalize this before the end of the month.

Thanks,
Daniel
Daniel Kim
Director, Procurement — OptiHealth
procurement@optihealth.com


From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@optihealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: termination rights + remedies beyond credits (SLA)

Hi Daniel — thanks for sending this over and for the context. We appreciate how critical latency is for OptiHealth.

We're going to run this up internally and come back with a commercial/legal compromise. In short: we can be flexible on a staged approach, but we have to balance operational risk, our standard liability caps, and the potential for over-triggering termination.

I've looped in Rishi (legal) and Ben (SE) to help scope SLO language and plausible thresholds. We'll aim to get a concrete counterproposal by EOD tomorrow.

Any specific durability/availability thresholds tied to your workflows (e.g., 99.95% monthly vs consecutive daily P99 violations) will help us calibrate.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: termination rights + remedies beyond credits (SLA)

Team — forwarding OptiHealth's ask. Key asks: termination right for repeated P99 misses; liquidated damages / fee-at-risk (they proposed up to 2x monthly committed fees). Attachment: OptiHealth_SLA_ask.xlsx.

My initial thoughts (open to edits):
- Don't give unconditional termination on a single SLO miss. Propose a staged ladder: credits first, then fee-at-risk (escrow or holdback of up to X% monthly fees), then termination only after repeated failures across two consecutive billing months and after a cure period.
- Cure period should be reasonable (30 days) and not retroactive. During cure Redwood can throttle/scale capacity or provide dedicated hours of operational support at no charge.
- Cap liability: propose cap = lesser of 6 months' committed fees or $500k; alternative cap = aggregated fees during the contract term. This keeps us from open-ended liquidated damages.
- Consider substitution: rather than all-cash liquidated damages, offer a partial buyout (one-time fee) and an option to convert to credits for a set period.

Ben — can you quantify how often we see tail latency P99 excursions at scale and whether a staged detection window (e.g., 5% of requests over X minutes) is feasible?
Rishi — can you draft a limited liability language and a 30-day cure + remediation plan. We should avoid language that allows immediate termination without cure.

If we can offer a clear, codified ladder with cure and caps, I think OptiHealth will accept something short of a full-liquidated-damages regime.

Thanks,
Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@optihealth.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, OptiHealth Procurement <procurement@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: termination rights + remedies beyond credits (SLA)

Daniel — thanks for the patience. Attached is a proposed redline (SLA_redlines.docx) that implements a compromise we discussed internally. High level summary of our counterproposal: 

- Staged remedies: (a) Service credits for isolated incidents; (b) Fee-at-risk holdback up to 25% of monthly committed fees if monthly availability/latency falls below the agreed threshold for two billing months; (c) Termination right for repeated material breaches, but only after: (i) written notice, (ii) 30-day cure period, and (iii) our remediation plan and at least one attempted mitigation (scale, dedicated capacity, or operational support).
- Liability cap: aggregate liability capped at the lesser of (i) six months of committed fees, or (ii) $400,000.
- Detection rules: P99 latency breach defined as 3+ days in a calendar month with P99 above the agreed threshold AND at least 5% of requests exceeding the threshold during those days. This reduces noise from short-lived spikes.
- Optional: For larger customers we can provide a dedicated capacity add-on (Dedicated) to meet stricter SLOs — this would remove the fee-at-risk holdback but move to a higher committed fee.

We believe this preserves OptiHealth's need for meaningful remedies while protecting Redwood from open-ended damages exposure and accidental termination triggers. Please see the attached redline for exact contract language. If this looks close we can circulate a DocuSign for signature once procurement confirms the cap and detection wording.

DocuSign (placeholder): https://docusign.com/envelope/status/ABC-123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Daniel Kim <daniel.kim@optihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: OptiHealth Procurement <procurement@optihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: termination rights + remedies beyond credits (SLA)

Marissa — thanks for the clear counter. The staged ladder + cure period is reasonable. Procurement wants to increase the cap to the lesser of 9 months' committed fees or $650,000 given the clinical risk, but is willing to accept the detection rule and the two-month repeat trigger.

Can you confirm whether Redwood would accept the higher cap as a carve-in for OptiHealth specifically (we're open to a term-limited exception) or if the six-month/$400k cap is a hard limit? If so, procurement will prepare the final SOW for signature.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Daniel
